dedupe_keys.name: internationally validated open indicators of large public urban green space for 13 cities supplementary materials

description: This data package supports the validation of open indicators of the availability and accessibility of large public urban green space in 13 diverse cities worldwide, published in Geographical Analysis on 15 September 2025. It was deposited in the RMIT University research repository by Ryan Turner, Carl Higgs, Vuokko Heikinheimo, Ruth Hunter, Júlio Celso Borello Vargas, Shiqin Liu, Eugen Resendiz and Geoff Boeing; the work was started by the Global Observatory of Healthy and Sustainable Cities for the 1000 Cities Challenge and the open-source Global Healthy and Sustainable City Indicators (GHSCI) software. It contains a Jupyter notebook that uses the Google Earth Engine API to filter public open space from GHSCI by vegetation index (NDVI) to identify large green spaces; one folder per city with shapefiles of the urban centre boundary, large green spaces, an accessibility grid and the pedestrian network; official local reference data for four cities; and an instructional video. Coverage: 13 cities. Access: RMIT repository (figshare), in four versions, one of them titled for healthy and climate resilient cities. Licence: CC BY-NC 4.0; free for non-commercial use. Caveats: the 13 city names were not listed in the metadata read. Simulation uses: green space access for heat and health planning. Related records: the 3-30-300 datasets.
